classification.difficultyReason: Identify each unit subdivision and read marked values; the hardest part requires interpreting negative thirds and expressing them correctly as negative mixed numbers.

content.prompt: Identify the numbers shown on these number lines. Give mixed numbers where appropriate.

spec.description: Double-ended number line labelled 7 to 12, subdivided into halves, with two red marked points.
spec.mathematics: Integer ticks at 7, 8, 9, 10, 11 and 12; half-unit subdivision ticks; points at 7.5 and 10.5.
spec.answerVisibility: Marked points are permanent givens; their numerical answers appear only in answer fields.

answer.worked:
Each whole is divided into two equal intervals. The points are halfway between $7$ and $8$, and between $10$ and $11$.

The numbers, from left to right, are $7\frac{1}{2}$ and $10\frac{1}{2}$.

spec.description: Double-ended number line labelled 0 to 5, subdivided into thirds, with three red marked points.
spec.mathematics: Every integer and third-unit subdivision tick is retained. Points are at 1+2/3, 2+1/3 and 4+2/3.
spec.answerVisibility: The numerical values of the marked points are withheld from the question diagram.

answer.worked:
Each interval represents $\frac{1}{3}$. Count the intervals after the preceding whole number:

$$\begin{align*}1+\frac{2}{3}&=1\frac{2}{3}\\2+\frac{1}{3}&=2\frac{1}{3}\\4+\frac{2}{3}&=4\frac{2}{3}\end{align*}$$

spec.description: Double-ended number line labelled 22 to 26 with fifth-unit subdivisions, continuing beyond 26, and four red marked points.
spec.mathematics: Fifth-unit ticks extend through 26.8. Marked points are 23+1/5, 24+2/5, 25+4/5 and 26+1/5.
spec.answerVisibility: All ticks, integer labels and marked points are visible; point values are answer-only.

answer.worked:
Each interval represents $\frac{1}{5}$. Count from the preceding whole number:

$$\begin{align*}23+\frac{1}{5}&=23\frac{1}{5}\\24+\frac{2}{5}&=24\frac{2}{5}\\25+\frac{4}{5}&=25\frac{4}{5}\\26+\frac{1}{5}&=26\frac{1}{5}\end{align*}$$

spec.description: Double-ended number line labelled −3, −2, −1 and 0, subdivided into thirds, with four red marked points.
spec.mathematics: Points lie at −7/3, −5/3, −2/3 and −1/3, in left-to-right order.
spec.answerVisibility: Negative integer labels and all marked points remain visible; the requested values appear only in answers.

answer.worked:
Each interval represents $\frac{1}{3}$. Moving right increases the value:

$$\begin{align*}-3+\frac{2}{3}&=-2\frac{1}{3}\\-2+\frac{1}{3}&=-1\frac{2}{3}\\-1+\frac{1}{3}&=-\frac{2}{3}\\-1+\frac{2}{3}&=-\frac{1}{3}\end{align*}$$

A leading minus applies to the whole mixed numeral: $-2\frac{1}{3}=-(2+\frac{1}{3})$.
